newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police arrest 7 in toxic contamination case.
newsitem.headline: German police arrest 7 in toxic contamination case.

text.p: Police have arrested seven people on suspicion of causing massive contamination of the environment by passing off highly toxic waste as harmless, German prosecutors said on Friday.
The arrests followed raids by 600 police on 140 buildings across Germany, seizing 8,000 files and otherb documents.

Frankfurt prosecutors' spokesman Rainer Schilling said they believed the suspects had set up firms in several German regions, portraying themselves as specialists in the field but then disposing of highly toxic waste cheaply and illegally.
The profits the companies made from their cut-price disposal methods ran into more than 10 million marks ($6.5 million), Schilling said.
"The exact extent of the ecological and financial damage caused by the suspects cannot yet be measured," he added.
Prosecutors believe the firms gathered toxic waste from across the country, collecting special bonuses for the disposal of particularly dangerous waste.

They then passed it off as low-grade oil waste and disposed of it in regular dumping sites, often far from where it had been collected. The group regularly visited sites in eastern Germany, Schilling said.

Investigators, who have been carrying out an undercover inquiry into the illegal network since last year, swooped on company depots and private homes on Thursday and Friday in locations including Frankfurt, Hamburg and Berlin.
The raids spanned all but two of Germany's 16 regional states. ($1=1.5250 Mark)
